title: Coxhead Academic Word List (AWL)
subtitle: Sublist 1: Core Cross-Disciplinary Academic Lexicon
citation: Averil Coxhead (2000), Victoria University of Wellington. 'A New Academic Word List', TESOL Quarterly, 34(2), 213-238.
description: The gold standard for academic English. Sublist 1 contains the highest-frequency academic word families identified across 3.5 million running words of peer-reviewed articles spanning Science, Law, Commerce, and Arts.

words.definition: To examine methodically and in detail the constitution or structure of something.
words.example: Researchers must analyze the experimental variance across clinical trials.

words.definition: A way of dealing with a situation or problem.
words.example: The committee adopted a multidisciplinary approach to solve urban traffic congestion.

words.definition: To evaluate or estimate the nature, ability, or quality of something.
words.example: Standardized metrics were implemented to assess student reading proficiency.

words.definition: To suppose to be the case without proof.
words.example: Economists often assume consumers make rational decisions under market constraints.

words.definition: The power or right to give orders, make decisions, and enforce obedience.
words.example: The federal regulatory authority approved the new environmental guidelines.

words.definition: To be a part of a whole; to combine to form an entirety.
words.example: Single-parent households constitute a growing proportion of the population.

words.definition: The circumstances that form the setting for an event, statement, or idea.
words.example: Quotations should always be evaluated within their historical context.

words.definition: To obtain something from a specified source or origin.
words.example: Many modern English terms derive from classical Greek and Latin roots.

words.definition: To point out or show evidence of something.
words.example: Initial quarterly reports indicate a steady rebound in retail consumer spending.

words.definition: To explain the meaning of information, words, or actions.
words.example: Historians continue to interpret the archival documents in contrasting ways.

words.definition: To move forward or carry on an action according to plan.
words.example: The engineering team will proceed with aerodynamic testing once safety clearances are granted.

words.definition: Sufficiently great or important to be worthy of attention; statistically noteworthy.
words.example: The randomized trial demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in symptoms.
